questions.e: Silent mode is explicitly not enough — switch off.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.q: The tutor says: 'Submit by 5 p.m. — the portal locks automatically.' After 5 p.m.:
questions.e: The portal locks — submission becomes impossible.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.q: You hear: 'Trains run every fifteen minutes from Platform 2.' A train just left at 9:00. The next train is at:
questions.e: Every 15 minutes: 9:00 → 9:15.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In IELTS Writing, Task 2 is worth:
questions.e: Task 2 carries double weight: two-thirds of the Writing band.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: What is the minimum word count for Writing Task 1?
questions.e: Task 1 requires at least 150 words.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: What is the minimum word count for Writing Task 2?
questions.e: Task 2 requires at least 250 words.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Recommended time for Task 1 is about:
questions.e: Spend ~20 minutes on Task 1 and ~40 on Task 2.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Which belongs in an Academic Task 1 report?
questions.e: Task 1 needs an overview of key trends — never opinions.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: A 'To what extent do you agree or disagree?' essay should:
o: Take one clear position and defend it
questions.e: Opinion essays need one clear, consistent position.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: A 'Discuss both views and give your opinion' essay needs:
o: One paragraph per view plus your opinion
questions.e: Cover both views, then state your own opinion.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In a formal GT letter, the correct greeting is:
questions.e: Formal letters open with 'Dear Sir or Madam,' (unknown recipient).

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In a formal letter, the matching sign-off is:
questions.e: 'Yours faithfully' pairs with 'Dear Sir or Madam'.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: A semi-formal letter to 'Dear Mr Brown' should close with:
questions.e: 'Yours sincerely' pairs with a named recipient (semi-formal/formal).

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Which sentence fits a formal complaint letter?
o: You guys messed up big time.
I would be grateful if you could issue a refund.
I want my money back now!
questions.e: Polite modal phrasing is correct for formal letters.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Covering every bullet point in a GT letter matters because:
o: Task Achievement requires addressing all parts
questions.e: Missing a bullet point directly lowers Task Achievement.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In Task 2, a new idea in the conclusion is:
o: A mistake — conclusions restate, not introduce
questions.e: Conclusions restate your position; new ideas belong in body paragraphs.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Memorised phrases like 'In the modern era' are:
questions.e: Examiners detect memorised language and penalise it.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: For a process diagram, the dominant voice is:
questions.e: Processes describe actions done to materials: passive voice dominates.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In a map description, 'adjacent to' means:
questions.e: 'Adjacent to' = next to / adjoining.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: A good Task 2 introduction does NOT:
questions.e: Examples belong in body paragraphs, not the introduction.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Which is a Task Response strength?
o: Fully answering every part of the question
questions.e: Task Response = fully addressing all parts of the prompt.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Cohesive devices should be:
questions.e: Natural, accurate cohesion scores; mechanical overuse lowers the band.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Under-length essays are penalised under:
questions.e: Word-count shortfalls hit Task Achievement/Response.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: A 'problem and solution' essay needs:
o: Problems and solutions in balanced paragraphs
questions.e: Answer both questions the prompt asks.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Writing 400 words in Task 2 is:
questions.e: Overlong essays multiply error chances; 270–300 words is safer.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In Task 1, comparing data within sentences:
o: Shows analytical skill and boosts scores
questions.e: Comparisons ('twice as many as') demonstrate analysis, not listing.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: The overview paragraph in Task 1 should:
questions.e: The overview captures main trends; details come later.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Proofreading Task 2 should focus on:
questions.e: Final minutes are for accuracy fixes, not new content.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In Speaking Part 1, ideal answers are:
o: 2–4 sentences with a reason or example
questions.e: Extend naturally: answer + reason + example.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In Part 2, the preparation time is:
questions.e: You get exactly 1 minute to prepare notes.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In Part 2, you should speak for:
questions.e: The long turn lasts 1–2 minutes.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Part 3 questions are:
questions.e: Part 3 discusses abstract ideas linked to the Part 2 topic.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: If you don't understand a Speaking question, you should:
o: Ask the examiner to repeat or rephrase
questions.e: Asking for repetition costs nothing; silence costs fluency evidence.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Memorised Speaking answers are:
questions.e: Examiners spot scripts instantly and penalise them.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Good pronunciation mainly means:
questions.e: Clarity and natural prosody matter — any accent is fine.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Self-correction in Speaking is:
questions.e: Occasional smooth self-correction is acceptable; stalling is not.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In Part 2, if you run out of things to say:
o: Keep going until the examiner stops you
questions.e: Stopping early caps your Fluency evidence — keep speaking.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Using varied tenses in Speaking shows:
questions.e: Range of tenses (past experiences, future speculation) demonstrates grammatical range.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In Part 3, good answers often:
questions.e: Part 3 expects abstract, general discussion with analysis.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Discourse markers like 'however' and 'as a result' help:
questions.e: They signal logical relationships, boosting Fluency & Coherence.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: The Speaking test is the same for:
questions.e: Speaking is identical across Academic and GT.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Recording yourself practising helps because:
o: You hear hesitations and errors you miss live
questions.e: Playback reveals fluency gaps you'd never notice while speaking.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Eye contact and a friendly tone in Speaking:
questions.e: They aren't separate criteria but support natural, confident delivery.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Unlike the paper test, the computer-delivered Listening test gives you only about two minutes _____ your answers at the end.
questions.e: A time phrase takes the infinitive of purpose: 'two minutes to check your answers'. 'For checking' would need no time phrase before it.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Despite _____ several full mock tests, Riya still felt nervous before the Speaking exam.
questions.e: Despite is followed by a gerund; the perfect gerund 'having completed' marks the action as finished before the main clause.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: The two charts _____ the changes in overseas travel habits over the past decade.
questions.e: The subject 'charts' is plural, so the verb is the plural present 'illustrate'. Task 1 overview sentences normally use simple present for describing visuals.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: The report notes a _____ in university applications from overseas, with numbers rising steadily since January.
questions.e: 'Rising steadily' signals growth: a surge is a sudden, strong increase. Slump, lull and halt all describe a drop or stop.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: A summary-completion task says 'NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS'. Which answer is acceptable even though the meaning is right in every option?
questions.e: Articles (a/the) do not count toward the word limit: 'the laboratory' counts as one word. Each other option has two or more content words.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.q: You hear: 'The library closes at seven — sorry, at half past six on weekdays.' The correct answer is:
questions.e: In IELTS Listening the speaker's correction always overrides the first statement: 'half past six' = 6:30. The 7:00 is a distractor.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: In Academic Writing Task 1, spending your first two minutes picking out trends pays off because:
o: examiners check your arithmetic on every figure
the overview needs 2–3 clear trends, not every figure
questions.e: Task 1 rewards selecting key features: a clear overview of 2–3 trends (no numbers) signals the selection skill examiners look for at Band 7+.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.q: In an IELTS Listening recording about energy, you hear: 'Electricity could meet 35 percent of global energy demand by twenty thirty-five.' The figure the speaker cites is:
questions.e: The speaker says '35 percent ... by twenty thirty-five' — the IEA's '35 by 35' target reported on 25 September 2026. Watch out: the numbers are easy to flip.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: Read the headline: 'World leaders approve UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise.' The statement 'The UN sea-level declaration was approved on 24 September 2026' is:
o: TRUE — UN News confirms leaders approved it at UNGA81 on 24 September 2026
FALSE — it was only drafted, not approved
NOT GIVEN — the date is not mentioned in the report
questions.e: UN News confirms world leaders approved the UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise on 24 September 2026 — so the statement is TRUE.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: In the sentence 'The world is set to overshoot the 1.5°C warming limit within the next few years,' the word 'overshoot' most nearly means:
questions.e: To overshoot means to go beyond or exceed a limit or target — key academic vocabulary for environment passages.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: A UN declaration on sea-level rise _____ by world leaders on 24 September 2026.
questions.e: A completed past event with a specific date needs the simple past passive: was approved.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: The UN Environment Programme _____ that the world will breach the 1.5°C limit within a few years.
questions.e: Recent news (23 September 2026) uses the present perfect: has warned — it reports the announcement, not just a finished past action.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.q: You hear: 'The outbreak has now affected 63 health zones across seven provinces.' How many provinces are affected?
questions.e: The figure 'seven' belongs to provinces; 63 is the number of health zones. IELTS Listening loves testing which number matches which noun.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: A Task 2 question reads: 'The use of artificial intelligence in education is increasing. Some argue it improves learning, while others fear it harms it. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.' The best approach is to:
o: discuss only the benefits to keep it simple
discuss both sides and state a clear personal position
write about unrelated technology to show range
questions.e: 'Discuss both views and give your own opinion' is a direct instruction: cover both sides AND take a clear position — otherwise you fail Task Response.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: In the headline 'WHO scales up its health response in Yemen,' the phrase 'scales up' means:
questions.e: To scale up means to increase or expand — a common collocation in news headlines about health, business and aid.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Australia _____ new migration rules for foreign students on 28 September 2026.
questions.e: A finished event pinned to a specific past date needs the simple past: announced. A fixed past-time marker rules out the present perfect here.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: (29 Sep 2026) In the headline 'Australia tightens student visa rules', the word 'tightens' is closest in meaning to:
questions.e: 'Tightens' here means strengthens restrictions — makes stricter. Relax is the opposite; broaden and postpone describe different changes.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: According to the 28 September report, the ballot for second- and third-year Working Holiday visas will offer unlimited second-year places. (TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN)
questions.e: FALSE: the report gives annual caps — up to 45,000 second-year and 5,000 third-year visas — so 'unlimited' directly contradicts the text.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: (29 Sep 2026) The report says 'dependants' of most student visa holders will face new restrictions. A 'dependant' in immigration English is:
o: a spouse or child attached to a visa holder
a university that sponsors the student
an English test the student must pass
questions.e: Dependants are family members — typically spouses or partners and dependent children — attached to the main visa holder. The 17 September announcement restricts exactly this group on most new student and graduate visas.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Australia plans to introduce a ballot for applicants _____ have completed the required regional work.
questions.e: The clause needs a relative pronoun for people: who. Which is for things, whose shows possession, and what cannot follow a noun as a relative.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: Australia aims to cut net overseas migration to 245,000 in 2026–27 and 225,000 in 2027–28. What does this suggest about the government's approach?
o: It wants greater control over migration numbers
It plans to end all temporary migration
It has abolished the Working Holiday programme
It will increase international student numbers
questions.e: The staged targets show the government seeking greater control over who enters and remains — the other options overstate or contradict the report.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: From 1 September 2026, Canada raised the study-permit proof of funds _____ CAD 23,448 for living expenses.
questions.e: 'Raise to' takes the new level as its object — raised ... to CAD 23,448. 'Raise by' would need the size of the increase.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: In the IELTS Voices 2026 report, Canada was the most common 'intended destination' among Indian respondents. 'Intended' here is closest in meaning to:
questions.e: 'Intended destination' = the place they plan to go. The report measured intentions and perceptions, not final decisions — a useful distinction for Reading inference questions.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: The IELTS Voices survey, _____ covered 8,395 test takers across 165 countries, found Canada leading among Indian respondents.
questions.e: Non-defining relative clause after a comma needs 'which' for things. 'That' cannot follow a comma in a non-defining clause.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: Indian students heading abroad are asked to register on the e-Videshi portal to access emergency consular support. A 'consular' service is one provided by:
questions.e: Consular services are provided by a country's embassies and consulates to its citizens abroad — exactly what the MEA's e-Videshi registration connects students to.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: UK study visas fell 16% in the year to June 2026. The number of visas issued _____ by 16% over that period.
questions.e: A finished past period ('in the year to June 2026') takes the simple past — fell. Present perfect would need an unfinished or present-linked timeframe.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: According to the IELTS Voices 2026 survey, 41% of study-focused Indian respondents intended to stay in their destination country for three to five years, compared with 26% of Chinese respondents. What can be inferred?
o: Indian students stay abroad longer than Chinese students in every case
A larger share of Indian than Chinese respondents planned medium-term stays
Most Indian students intend to settle abroad permanently
Chinese students prefer Canada over Australia
questions.e: Only the comparison is supported: 41% vs 26% for three-to-five-year stays. 'Every case' and 'most' overstate the data, and the survey said nothing about Chinese destination preferences.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: The number of international applicants ___ risen steadily over the past year.
questions.e: The subject is 'number' (singular), so 'has' is correct - a classic IELTS trap.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: The company decided to ___ the product launch until safety checks were complete.
questions.e: 'Shelve' means to put aside or postpone - the launch was postponed until checks finished.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: She has been living in Pune ___ 2019.
questions.e: 'Since' is used with a point in time (2019); 'for' needs a duration.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: A ___ in the river embankment caused flooding in the nearby villages.
questions.e: A 'breach' is a break or gap - here, in the embankment holding back the river.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: The passage states that EOS-05, launched 4 September 2026, is India's first imaging satellite designed for geosynchronous orbit. This statement is:
questions.e: The passage explicitly reports EOS-05 as India's first imaging satellite designed for geosynchronous orbit.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: The two countries agreed to show greater ___ towards each other's concerns.
questions.e: The noun 'sensitivity' fits after 'greater'; 'sensitive' is the adjective form.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: By the time the results are announced, she ___ for the exam for six months.
questions.e: 'By the time' + future point calls for the future perfect continuous: 'will have been preparing'.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: The data suggests the hikes will continue
The datas suggests the hikes will continue
The data suggest the hikes will continue
The datas suggest the hikes will continue
questions.e: 'Data' is plural in formal academic English; the verb must agree: 'the data suggest'.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: In the passage, the phrase 'terminal repo rate' most nearly means:
o: The rate at which banks lend to each other overnight
The peak level the policy rate reaches in a hiking cycle
The rate on terminal-year government bonds
A penalty rate for late repayments
questions.e: In the context of BofA's forecast of hikes 'through H1 2027', the terminal rate is the cycle's peak — 6.25%.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Identify the error: 'Despite of the rate hikes, consumption remained strong.'
questions.e: 'Despite' never takes 'of' — the correct form is 'Despite the rate hikes, ...'.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: The word 'greenshoe' in the Blue Bond announcement refers to:
o: An option to increase the issue size
questions.e: A green-shoe option lets the issuer increase the issue size; here Rs 500 crore over the Rs 600 crore base.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: The noun 'quintal' refers to:
o: a unit of weight equal to 100 kilograms
questions.e: A quintal is 100 kg — don't confuse it with 'quintile', one-fifth of a distribution.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Choose the correct spelling:
questions.e: 'Battery' has two t's; PM-DHARA funds intra-state transmission networks with battery storage.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: In archery reporting, a 'shoot-off' is:
questions.e: A shoot-off decides tied archery matches — India beat South Korea 158-157 in one at the Asian Games.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: The word 'pendency' in the Special Campaign 6.0 announcement most nearly means:
questions.e: The campaign targets reducing pendency — work that is pending or unfinished across ministries.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Identify the error: 'The bloc demanded for a return to paper ballots.'
questions.e: 'Demand' is transitive — it never takes 'for': 'demanded a return to paper ballots'.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Sabha' in 'gram sabha' means:
questions.e: Gram sabha is the assembly of voters in a village (Article 243A of the Constitution).

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: A 'basis point' equals:
questions.e: 100 basis points = 1 percentage point; a 25 bps hike takes the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.50%.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: The 46th Chess Olympiad was held in:
questions.e: Samarkand, Uzbekistan — September 2026; India won Open silver and defended the combined trophy.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: Who inaugurated 'Reform Utsav' on 2 October 2026?
questions.e: PM Modi inaugurated the campaign, which marks 12 years of transformative governance.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Pendency' refers to:
questions.e: Pendency = matters awaiting decision or disposal; Special Campaign 6.0 targets it.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: August 2026 CPI inflation was:
questions.e: 4.82% — the third straight month above the RBI's 4% medium-term target.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Step down' most nearly means:
questions.e: 'Step down' — resign from a position.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Smriti Mandhana ___ appointed captain on 6 October.
questions.e: 'Was' — singular subject, past passive.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: The country that signed pacts with India in October 2026 is:
questions.e: Pacts on migration, young professionals, transport and research.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: A 25 bps 'hike' in the repo rate means the rate:
questions.e: 'Hike' = an increase.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: The repo rate ___ raised to 5.50%.
questions.e: 'Was' — singular subject, past passive.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: The SME Growth Fund's government commitment is:
questions.e: Rs 10,000 crore to an AIF, approved by the Cabinet on 6 October 2026.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: ITLA will function as:
o: an SPV and apex body for transport planning
questions.e: The Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority was approved as a Special Purpose Vehicle.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: JOSH teams were launched at:
questions.e: Health Minister J.P. Nadda launched them at Bharat Mandapam on 8 October 2026.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: Which state became India's sixth fully literate state?
questions.e: Declared on 6 October 2026 under NEP 2020 and the ULLAS programme.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to:
questions.e: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai, for asymmetric organic synthesis.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Catalyse' most nearly means:
questions.e: To catalyse = to speed up or trigger; the SME fund aims to catalyse growth capital.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Denotify' most nearly means:
questions.e: Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar as a protest site in October 2026 — removing its official status as a designated demonstration venue.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Culminate' most nearly means:
questions.e: A useful academic word: tensions culminated in the October 2026 protests, which in turn led to the Jantar Mantar denotification.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Volatility' most nearly means:
questions.e: Volatility is rapid unpredictable fluctuation. On 13 October 2026, FM Nirmala Sitharaman said the RBI would sustain measures against excessive rupee volatility.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Hedging' (finance) most nearly means:
questions.e: Hedging protects against risk. The RBI's 12 October 2026 circular restricts INR non-deliverable derivative contracts for non-residents to hedging purposes only.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Deputation' most nearly means:
questions.e: Deputation is temporary assignment. The CAPF (General Administration) Act, 2026 reserves 50% of Inspector General posts for IPS deputation.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: Apple's HomeView smart home hub can recognise up to ten individual faces. True or False?
questions.e: False — HomeView, announced 13 October 2026, recognises up to six individual faces and shows each a personalised display.

questions.subject: English
questions.q:
Statement: The RBI cut the repo rate in October 2026.
Classify as TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
questions.e: FALSE — the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 October 2026.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In the phrase ‘soaring inflation’, the word ‘soaring’ is closest in meaning to:
questions.e: ‘Soaring’ means rising very quickly — ‘rapidly increasing’.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: By the time the detailed notification was issued, applications ______ already opened.
questions.e: The past perfect ‘had’ is needed for the earlier of two past events: ‘had already opened’.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ULLAS, under which Lakshadweep was declared 100% literate, is a programme for:
questions.e: ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society) is the national adult-literacy programme.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: A ‘landmark’ decision is one that is:
o: historic and marking a turning point
questions.e: ‘Landmark’ describes something historic, marking an important turning point.

questions.subject: Test Updates
questions.q: From when is IELTS in India fully computer-based?
questions.e: September 2026 - IDP Education discontinued the paper-based test in India.

questions.subject: Test Updates
questions.q: When was the last paper-based IELTS test in India before the format was phased out?
questions.e: The final three paper tests were 25 July, 6 August and 22 August 2026.

questions.subject: Test Updates
questions.q: In which country is the paper-based Writing hybrid option available from October 2026?
questions.e: Bangladesh - British Council's hybrid IELTS on Computer with handwritten Writing.

questions.subject: Test Updates
questions.q: What is the total duration of the IELTS test?
questions.e: 2 hours 45 minutes - unchanged under computer delivery.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: Choose the correct verb form: She _____ at the hospital since 2019.
questions.e: With 'since 2019', the present perfect continuous ('has been working') correctly expresses an action that started in the past and continues to the present.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to UBIQUITOUS:
questions.e: 'Ubiquitous' means appearing or found everywhere.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q: Passage: About 71% of the Earth's surface is covered by water, most of it in the oceans. Question: More than 80% of the Earth's surface is covered by water. (True / False / Not Given)
questions.e: The statement claims more than 80%, but the passage states 'about 71%' — the claim is directly contradicted by the passage, so the answer is FALSE.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.q: Listening: You hear 'The seminar is scheduled for the twenty-second of October, twenty twenty-six.' Which date should you write?
questions.e: In the IELTS Listening test, dates, numbers and spellings must be written exactly as heard; 'the twenty-second of October, twenty twenty-six' = 22 October 2026.

questions.subject: Writing & Speaking
questions.q: Writing Task 2: Which sentence best paraphrases 'Unemployment among graduates is rising because the number of qualified candidates exceeds available positions'?
o: There are not enough jobs for graduates
There are more qualified graduates than the job market can absorb
Graduates should not apply for jobs
The job market is unfair to graduates
questions.e: Effective paraphrasing restates the idea with different words and structure while keeping the meaning — option 2 does this; option 1 changes the meaning (not enough jobs vs too many qualified people).

questions.subject: Speaking
questions.q: West Indies won the 4th T20I against India on 14 October 2026 at:
questions.e: West Indies 247/3 beat India 223 by 24 runs at Hyderabad; the series is level 2–2 and the decider is in Bengaluru on 17 October 2026.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: 'Prolific' in the sentence 'Shai Hope continued his prolific run on the tour' most nearly means:
questions.e: 'Prolific' = producing a great number or amount; here, Hope's second century of the series (102* off 50 balls) — his third T20I hundred, passing Chris Gayle's West Indies record.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.q:
On 15 October 2026, five projects worth about Rs. 3,350 crore were dedicated in Ladakh, including a new airport terminal at Leh, the 298-km Nimmu–Padum–Darcha road, the 9 MW Hanu hydro project, 40 water bodies in 40 villages under Project Him Sarovar, and a conservation park for rock art.

Which project is aimed at protecting ancient rock art?
o: The Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat, Leh
questions.e: India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat, Leh, protects Ladakh's ancient rock art and promotes responsible heritage tourism.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: She has been working at this hospital ___ 2019.
questions.e: With a specific starting point in time, use 'since' 2019.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: The results of the trial were quite ___, exceeding even the most optimistic expectations.
questions.e: Results exceeding expectations are remarkable — worthy of attention.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: If I ___ more free time, I would travel around the world.
questions.e: This is a second conditional (unreal present): 'If I had' more free time, I would travel.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: Due to the speaker's illness, the meeting has been ___ until next Monday.
questions.e: Moving an event to a later date is to postpone it.

questions.subject: Grammar
questions.q: He is responsible ___ managing the department's annual budget.
questions.e: The correct collocation is 'responsible for' doing something.

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.q: The new safety regulations will come ___ effect from the first of next month.
questions.e: The fixed phrase is 'come into effect'.

questions.subject: IELTS
questions.q: Which of the following is true of IELTS in 2026?
o: The test is now fully paper-based
Paper-based tests are discontinued; the test is computer-delivered with a face-to-face Speaking interview
Results are announced the same day
questions.e: IELTS moved to fully computer-delivered testing from mid-2026, while the Speaking section remains a face-to-face (or video) interview with a human examiner. Results take 3-5 days.

questions.subject: IELTS
questions.q: The standard IELTS fee in India from 1 April 2026 is:
questions.e: The IELTS fee in India rose from Rs. 18,000 to Rs. 19,000 on 1 April 2026. Always confirm at the official portal before paying.

capsules.subject: Reading
capsules.title: Governor reshuffle across six states (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: On 12 October 2026, President Droupadi Murmu announced a governor reshuffle: Braj Mohan Ram to Odisha, Dr Sudha Yadav to Karnataka, Dr Dhal Singh Bisen to Uttarakhand and Dushyant Gautam to Sikkim. Om Prakash Mathur was transferred from Sikkim to Kerala, and Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was appointed Governor of Tamil Nadu.

capsules.subject: Test Updates
capsules.title: IELTS in India fully computer-based from Sep 2026
capsules.body: IELTS in India is fully computer-delivered from September 2026 - IDP Education discontinued the paper-based test across the country. The last paper-based tests were held on 25 July, 6 August and 22 August 2026.

capsules.subject: Test Updates
capsules.title: Paper-based Writing returns as hybrid option in Bangladesh
capsules.body: From October 2026, British Council is reintroducing paper-based Writing as a hybrid option with IELTS on Computer in Bangladesh: Listening and Reading on computer, Writing answers handwritten on the official answer sheet, Speaking face-to-face - and the certificate does not mention the paper module.

capsules.subject: IELTS
capsules.title: IELTS in 2026: fully computer-delivered, Rs. 19,000 fee in India
capsules.body: IELTS has transitioned to a fully computer-delivered format from mid-2026 (paper-based tests discontinued), though Speaking remains a face-to-face interview. Scores range 0-9 in half bands; the fee in India rose to Rs. 19,000 on 1 April 2026; results take 3-5 days and scores are valid two years.
